name: Sec cost estimates

subjectOf.text: Measured against this study's survey data, the SEC marginally overestimated the cost of the initial Form PF filing for both annually filing smaller advisers and quarterly filing larger advisers.
subjectOf.abstract: The cross-comparison suggests that the SEC may be marginally overestimating the cost of Form PF filings for both annually filing smaller private fund advisers and quarterly filing larger private fund advisers.
subjectOf.citation: Wulf A. Kaal, Private Fund Disclosures Under the Dodd-Frank Act (2014). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=2447306
scope_conditions: comparison with SEC estimates in 76 Fed. Reg. 71128-01
data for larger advisers rests on a small sample

subjectOf.text: For quarterly filing larger private fund advisers, the SEC substantially overestimated the cost of subsequent Form PF filings; the survey's estimate is roughly half of what the SEC projected.
subjectOf.abstract: With regards to quarterly filing larger private fund advisers, however, the SEC appears to be substantially overestimating the cost of subsequent Form PF filings.
subjectOf.citation: Wulf A. Kaal, Private Fund Disclosures Under the Dodd-Frank Act (2014). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=2447306
scope_conditions: subsequent Form PF filings by large advisers
based on a small sample of larger advisers

subjectOf.text: The SEC's error runs in the opposite direction for small advisers on recurring filings: the agency marginally underestimated the cost of subsequent Form PF filings for annually filing smaller private fund advisers.
subjectOf.abstract: The cross-comparison suggests that the SEC may be marginally underestimating the cost of Form PF filings for annually filing smaller private fund advisers.
subjectOf.citation: Wulf A. Kaal, Private Fund Disclosures Under the Dodd-Frank Act (2014). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=2447306
scope_conditions: subsequent Form PF filings by annually filing smaller advisers
